pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: For an operating lease, the leased physical asset appears on the balance sheet of:
option_a: neither the lessor nor the lessee.
option_b: the lessor.
option_c: the lessee.
explanation_en: With an operating lease, the actual leased asset remains on the lessor's balance sheet and the lessor recognizes depreciation expense on the asset. The lessee is required to recognize an asset and a liability equal to the present value of the promised lease payments.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: For an operating lease, the lessor must disclose:
option_a: interest recognized in the income statement relating to the lease receivable asset.
option_b: impairments of the leased asset.
option_c: selling profit or loss on derecognition of the leased asset.
explanation_en: Because the leased asset remains on the lessor's balance sheet for an operating lease, the lessor must disclose impairments of the asset. The other choices refer to lessor disclosures for finance leases.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: When a lessee recognizes a balance sheet asset and liability for a new lease:
option_a: the liability is typically greater than the asset.
option_b: the asset and liability are equal.
option_c: the asset is typically greater than the liability.
explanation_en: At the initiation of a lease, the lessee records an asset and a liability that are both equal to the present value of the promised lease payments.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: An airline leases a new airplane from its manufacturer for 10 years. For financial reporting, the airline must record an asset and a liability on its balance sheet:
option_a: only if the lease is a nance lease.
option_b: only if the lease is an operating lease.
option_c: regardless of whether the lease is a nance or operating lease.
explanation_en: For both finance and operating leases, both IFRS and U.S. GAAP require an asset and a liability to be recorded on the lessee's balance sheet, unless the lease is short-term or (under IFRS) for a low-value asset.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: An employer offers a defined benefit pension plan and a defined contribution pension plan. The employer's balance sheet is most likely to present an asset or liability related to:
option_a: the dened benet plan.
option_b: the dened contribution plan.
option_c: both of these pension plans.
explanation_en: Only a defined benefit plan has a funded status that would appear on the balance sheet as an asset or liability. Employer payments into a defined contribution plan are recognized as expenses in the period incurred.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: A lease is most likely to be reported as a finance lease when:
option_a: the present value of the lease payments is less than the asset’s fair value.
option_b: ownership of the leased asset transfers to the lessee.
option_c: the lessor would otherwise operate the asset in its normal course of business.
explanation_en: A lease is reported as a finance lease when ownership of the leased asset transfers to the lessee. Among the other conditions for a finance lease are that the present value of the lease payments is greater than or equal to the asset's fair value, and that the lessor has no other use for the asset.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: Which of the following regarding employer contributions is least likely a required disclosure under IFRS?
option_a: Expected employer contributions for the next period for defined benefit plans.
option_b: Total employer’s contributions expensed in the income statement for defined contribution plans.
option_c: Reasons for changes in employer contributions for defined contribution plans.
explanation_en: Minimum disclosure requirements for defined benefit plans include expected future employer contributions. The only disclosure required for defined contribution plans is the separate disclosure of the employer's contribution expensed in the income statement. No further disclosure regarding changes in employer contributions is required.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: Which of the following is least likely included in the disclosures for share-based compensation reporting?
option_a: Share price at the reporting date.
option_b: Impact of share-based transactions on the balance sheet.
option_c: How the fair value at the grant date was determined.
explanation_en: The required disclosures are the nature of the plan as well as key details such as grant date, vesting date, service period, and settlement characteristics; how the fair value at the grant date was determined; and the effect on earnings and the financial position (i.e., income statement and balance sheet). Share price at the reporting date is not a required disclosure, although it may be helpful for the users' understanding.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: Under which reporting standards are share-based compensation expensed to the income statement over the vesting period?
option_a: IFRS, but not U.S. GAAP.
option_b: U.S. GAAP, but not IFRS.
option_c: Both IFRS and U.S. GAAP.
explanation_en: Both IFRS and U.S. GAAP require companies to estimate the fair value of share-based compensation at the grant date and to expense it to the income statement over the vesting period.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: Which of the following is most accurate regarding financial reporting of an operating lease from a lessor's perspective?
option_a: The lessor recognizes the lease payments as income.
option_b: At lease inception, the lessor removes the asset from the balance sheet.
option_c: The lessor does not record the depreciation expense.
explanation_en: For an operating lease, the lessor reports the lease payments as income. The lessor does not remove the leased asset from the balance sheet and continues to record the depreciation expense over the life of the asset.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: When the risks of ownership of an asset are not substantially transferred to the lessee, a lease is most likely to be reported as:
option_a: a nance lease.
option_b: an operating lease.
option_c: an investing lease.
explanation_en: Both the lessee and lessor report a lease as an operating lease when the risks of ownership are not substantially transferred to the lessee.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: A lessor will remove the leased asset from its balance sheet and record interest income from the lease only if the lease is classified as:
option_a: an operating lease.
option_b: a sales-type lease.
option_c: a nance lease.
explanation_en: Under IFRS and U.S. GAAP, a lessor will classify a lease as either an operating lease or a finance lease. If it is classified as a finance lease, the leased asset is removed from the lessor's balance sheet and interest income is recognized over the life of the lease. A sales- type lease is a classification under U.S. GAAP that does not affect the accounting treatment.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: A lessor retains the leased asset on its balance sheet for:
option_a: neither nance leases not operating leases.
option_b: nance leases, but not operating leases.
option_c: operating leases, but not nance leases.
explanation_en: For an operating lease, the lessor retains the leased asset on its balance sheet and recognizes depreciation expense over its life. For a finance lease, the lessor removes the leased asset from its balance sheet and recognizes a lease receivable.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: A lessee is most likely to be required to classify a lease as a finance lease if:
option_a: the lease is long term.
option_b: the sum of the lease payments is equal to the value of the leased asset.
option_c: the lessor has no other use for the asset.
explanation_en: A lessee is required to classify a lease as a finance lease if the lessor has no other use for the asset. Long-term leases can be either operating or finance leases. A lease must be classified as a finance lease if the present value of the lease payments is equal to or greater than the value of the leased asset.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: For a lessee, the portion of a lease payment that represents repayment of principal is a cash flow from:
option_a: operations.
option_b: nancing.
option_c: investing.
explanation_en: The principal portion of a lease payment is a financing outflow on the lessee's cash flow statement. The interest portion is an operating cash outflow under U.S. GAAP and may be treated as an operating or financing outflow under IFRS.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: For a long-term lease, the amount recorded initially by the lessee as a liability is:
option_a: the present value of the lease payments.
option_b: the total of the lease payments.
option_c: the fair value of the leased asset.
explanation_en: With a finance lease, both an asset and liability are reported on the lessee's balance sheet, equal to the present value of the promised lease payments.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 36 Topics in Long-Term Liabilities and Equity
question_en: Which of the following must both the lessee and lessor disclose under IFRS 16?
option_a: Restrictions and covenants imposed by the lease.
option_b: Interest expense included in the income statement resulting from the lease.
option_c: Maturity analysis of future payments.
explanation_en: Both the lessee and lessor are required to disclose a maturity analysis of the lease liabilities (lessee) and lease payments receivable (lessor). Only the lessee must disclose the restrictions and covenants imposed by the lease. The lessee will disclose the interest expense resulting from the lease; the lessor will disclose the interest income.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes
question_en: Which of the following statements about tax deferrals is NOT correct?
option_a: A deferred tax liability is expected to result in future cash outow.
option_b: Income tax paid can include payments or refunds for other years.
option_c: Taxes payable are determined by pretax income and the tax rate.
explanation_en: Taxes payable are the taxes due to the government and are determined by taxable income and the tax rate. Note that pretax income is income before tax expense and is used for financial reporting. Taxable income is the income based upon IRS rules that determines taxes due and is used for tax reporting.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes
question_en: If a firm uses accelerated depreciation for tax purposes and straight-line depreciation for financial reporting, which of the following results is least likely?
option_a: A permanent dierence will result between tax and nancial reporting.
option_b: A temporary dierence will result between tax and nancial reporting.
option_c: Income tax expense will be greater than taxes payable.
explanation_en: A permanent difference between tax and financial reporting is a difference that is expected to not reverse itself. Under normal circumstances, the effects of the different depreciation methods will reverse.

pdf: D:\CLAUDE\Projet CFA\CFA L1\2. QB KAPLAN-3000 MCQs\QSTN WITH ANS\Financial statement analysis\Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes - Answers.pdf
subtopic: Reading 37 Analysis of Income Taxes
question_en: A tax loss carryforward is best described as the:
option_a: net taxable loss that can be used to reduce taxable income in the future.
option_b: net taxable loss that can be used to recover taxes paid previously.
option_c: dierence between deferred tax liabilities and deferred tax assets.
explanation_en: A tax loss carryforward is the net taxable loss that can be used to reduce taxable income in the future.
